oracle.description: templates/dispatch/hooks/tests/test-artifacts-root.sh decides correctness: REQ-006..REQ-011, and nothing outside log-session-cost.sh. Written from the spec row by an author with no access to any implementation. agentops.hooks.tests is carried as a non-starts_red guard so the rest of the telemetry surface cannot regress unnoticed.

purpose: Make templates/dispatch/hooks/log-session-cost.sh read its AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT default from one place instead of hardcoding it. Today line 57 is export AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT="${AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT:-/projects/dev}", and the same literal is written again in templates/dispatch/scripts/dispatch_release.py; the comment beside each points at the other as the reason it exists, which is how two copies of a path drift. The single source is the data file templates/dispatch/artifacts-root.default, which already exists and holds one line. Change the two lines that establish the root and nothing else. An AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT already in the environment must still win. With it unset, the hook must export the value read from that data file, resolved RELATIVE TO THE HOOK'S OWN LOCATION -- not to the working directory and not to a hardcoded absolute path. This matters because the hooks are symlinked into /projects/dev/.claude/hooks/, so a hook invoked through the symlink sees the symlink path in BASH_SOURCE and a plain dirname finds the wrong directory; resolve the real path first. If the data file is missing or empty the hook must still exit 0 and still write its cost record -- a hook must never fail its caller because a defaults file went away; what it does about the root in that case is your choice. Leave the cost-log default on line 19 and the gate-log default on line 20 byte-identical: they are different defaults with different owners and are not this packet's business. Everything else about the hook is untouched -- the JSON record's field names, order and types, AGENTOPS_COST_LOG, the auditctl workflow.session write, the max-per-session semantics, and exiting 0 in every case.
required_outcomes: with it unset the root comes from templates/dispatch/artifacts-root.default
the data file is found relative to the hook's real location, including through a symlink and from any working directory
a missing or empty data file still leaves the hook exiting 0 with its cost record written
the cost-log and gate-log defaults are unchanged
every assertion the T-1/T-4 telemetry oracle already made still holds

acceptance_properties.fails_when: the hook overrides an AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT already set in the environment

acceptance_properties.requirement: the default comes from the data file
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the exported root does not equal the contents of templates/dispatch/artifacts-root.default

acceptance_properties.requirement: resolution follows the hook, not the caller
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the hook fails to resolve the file from a foreign working directory or when invoked through a symlink

acceptance_properties.requirement: the root is not written down twice
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a line mentioning AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT still contains a hardcoded path

acceptance_properties.requirement: the neighbouring defaults are left alone
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the cost-log or gate-log default line changes

acceptance_properties.requirement: a missing defaults file never fails the caller
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the hook exits non-zero or writes no cost record when the data file is absent

acceptance_properties.requirement: the rest of the telemetry surface is untouched
acceptance_properties.fails_when: any assertion the T-1/T-4 telemetry or maintain-check oracle already made regresses

non_goals: the driver's copy of the default, which is M-6b
the auditctl drain and the record's shape
